```{r}
data <- read.csv("data/students.csv")
summary(data)
```


```{r}
## imput tidyverse formule
library(tidyverse)
```
```{r}
data %>% ## add table 
  summarise_if(is.numeric, list( ##numeric
    mean = mean,
    sd = sd,
    median = median,
    quantile = quantile,
    min = min,
    max = max
  ), na.rm = TRUE) ## skip the missing values
```


```{r}
## the summary is different from one column to the next because the column with not the same type of character
```
```{r}
summary(data)
```



```{r}
library(tidyverse)

students <- read_csv("data/students.csv")

# Histogramme de la variable Weight with copilot 
hist(data$Weight,
     main = "weight histogram",
     xlab = "weight",
     col = "blue",
     border = "black")
```
```
```{r}
```{r}
# Densité de la variable Weight with copilot 
plot(density(data$Weight, na.rm = TRUE),
     main = "Weight densitogram",
     xlab = "Weight",
     ylab = "Density",
     col = "blue",
     lwd = 2)
```
```
```{r}
```{r}
# Boxplot de la variable Weight with chat gpt
boxplot(data$Weight,
        main = "weight Boxplot",
        ylab = "weight",
        col = 'blue')
```
```{r}
## with chatgpt method of the histogram and not copilot
ggplot(students, aes(x = Weight, fill = Gender)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 1, color = "white", alpha = 0.7, position = "identity") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("F" = "lightcoral", "M" = "steelblue")) +
  labs(title = "Histogram of Weight by Gender",
       x = "Weight (kg)",
       y = "Count",
       fill = "Gender") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 14)
```
```{r}
## same methode with copilot
boxplot(Weight ~ Gender, data = data,
        main = "weight Boxplot",
        xlab = "gender",
        ylab = "weight",
        col = c('pink',"blue"))
```
```{r}
library(effectsize)

# Make sure Gender is a factor
data$Gender <- as.factor(data$Gender)

# Run Wilcoxon test
res <- wilcox.test(Weight ~ Gender, data = data, exact = FALSE, correct = FALSE)
print(res)

# Extract group sizes
n1 <- sum(data$Gender == levels(data$Gender)[1])
n2 <- sum(data$Gender == levels(data$Gender)[2])

# U statistic from Wilcoxon test
U <- res$statistic

# Expected value and standard deviation of U
mu <- n1 * n2 / 2
sigma <- sqrt(n1 * n2 * (n1 + n2 + 1) / 12)

# Z value
Z <- (U - mu) / sigma

# Rank-biserial correlation
r <- Z / sqrt(n1 + n2)
r

```
